## 3a379d1ed52c

**Possible shortcut / domain undercoverage:** “complete only isolated 3-cell blue connected components whose bounding box is 2×2.”

That rival fits all 4/4 canonical demonstrations. The current sampler also cannot distinguish it from the intended “scan every 2×2 window containing exactly three blue cells and one zero” rule: over 300 default samples (seeds 0–99 in each of easy/medium/hard, sample index `seed % 11`), every blue component had size 3 and no triggering 2×2 windows overlapped. See `checks/audit/3a379d1ed52c/sampler-census.json`.

An exact 5×5 counterexample is retained in `checks/audit/3a379d1ed52c/finding.json`. It contains one connected 6-cell blue object with overlapping qualifying windows. The implemented `self_check` accepts it (`[]`), although it lies outside the documented “target windows are separated” sampler subset. The canonical Racket authority (rule hash `bc3677d36da1`, generator SHA `50370c6aa514c74f1d3c6d87e2c82e365325eb813367838d579a8cab86fd41c9`) fills cells `(0,2)` and `(2,2)` green; the isolated-component rival fills neither. Official output and hashes are in `checks/audit/3a379d1ed52c/racket.json`, with the rival in `checks/audit/3a379d1ed52c/rival.json`.

This is a **possible shortcut**, not a claim that the current canonical query is mislabeled. The actionable concern is that the generator's narrow sampler and weak validator provide no teaching evidence for the written window-scanning generalization.
